names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 27 iulie, «Sfântul Clement, Arhiepiscopul Ohridei», with the rank and the see left off.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 22 Νοεμβρίου, «Άγιος Κλήμης ο Θαυματουργός επίσκοπος Αχρίδας της Βουλγαρίας», with the rank word, the epithet and the see left off.

death.note: doxologia.ro: «A fondat în Ohrida Mănăstirea „Sfântul Pantelimon”, unde a fost îngropat în anul 916 într-un sicriu pe care l-a făcut cu mâinile sale.» — the year is of his burial, which is the only year the page gives.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 27 iulie — «Sfântul Clement, Arhiepiscopul Ohridei»

attestations.note: The same page says he is kept «în data de 25 noiembrie, ziua adormirii sale, precum și pe 27 iulie». One row per church is the schema, so the November day is recorded here and he renders on 27 July, the day this calendar was read on.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 22ης Νοεμβρίου — «Άγιος Κλήμης ο Θαυματουργός επίσκοπος Αχρίδας της Βουλγαρίας»

attestations.note: The life page `https://www.saint.gr/3073/saint.aspx` heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 22 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», and the man is the folder's own: ordained bishop for Bulgaria by Methodius, builder of the monastery of Saint Panteleimon at Ohrid where his relics were laid. **The folder's Romanian row keeps him on 27 July and this Greek row keeps him on 22 November, and that is not a second commemoration being invented**: they are two churches' days, one row each, which is the schema. The folder's existing death interval from doxologia is not replaced; the page gives no year of its own, only the reign of the emperor Michael, 842 to 867, son of Theophilos the iconoclast. The page adds that the saint's head is at the monastery of the Honourable Forerunner at Veroia. No hymn. No asterisk and not the sentence «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη η ύπαρξη του Αγίου».
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).
